title: Neon Velocity: Skyline Run
premise: A futuristic courier sprints automatically across glowing sky rails above a neon city, surviving as long as possible by timing jumps over gaps and recovering with a second midair jump.
interaction_model: One-button endless runner with tap, click, Space, or Up Arrow input for jump; supports double jump and automatic forward motion.
objective: Stay on the floating rails, avoid falling into the void, and push the run's distance score as high as possible.
progression: The run begins gently, then continuously speeds up while randomized platform gaps and heights demand faster reactions; checkpoints are acknowledged through audio and visual feedback every 100 meters.
mood: Energetic, sleek, arcade-like, and slightly tense
likely_audience: Players who enjoy accessible reflex games, endless runners, mobile-friendly arcade loops, and neon cyber-style presentation.
confidence_notes: High confidence that the game is an endless runner centered on survival distance.
High confidence that double jump is the signature mechanic.
Medium confidence on fiction details such as whether the rails represent rooftops, transit lanes, or suspended platforms, since the story framing is light.
High confidence that the intended fantasy is a stylish futuristic courier run through a skyline at night.
recreation_prompt: Create a polished browser-based arcade game called "Neon Velocity: Skyline Run" in which a futuristic courier automatically runs across glowing floating rails above a neon nighttime city. The player should control only jumping using tap, mouse click, Space, or Up Arrow, and the character must be able to double jump before landing. Structure the game as an endless survival run: the world scrolls left, the runner stays near the left side of the screen, platforms spawn endlessly with randomized widths, gaps, and slight height variation, and the run ends instantly if the character falls below the screen into the void. Make distance traveled the main score, shown in a compact HUD in meters, and gradually increase game speed over time so the challenge escalates naturally. Include a strong neon presentation with a dark purple-blue sky gradient, drifting stars, a glowing moon haze, parallax skyline silhouettes, luminous rail edges, a cute stylized runner avatar, trailing motion glow, and small particle bursts on jumping and landing. Add a start screen with title, subtitle, character flavor text, and controls, plus a game-over overlay showing final distance and a restart button. Support upbeat looping background music and short sound effects for start, jump, landing, checkpoints, button clicks, and failure. Reinforce feedback with brief animated reaction badges for jump boosts, milestones, and crashes. The overall tone should feel sleek, energetic, readable on mobile and desktop, and easy to learn but increasingly hard to sustain through timing and double-jump mastery.
